metadata.source: Derived from architecture-review-board policies.json (Cloud Security Directive, 20 policies)
metadata.note: Each rule uses SemanticFunctions.MatchesAnyMeaning at threshold 0.55 with gateThreshold 0.45 to fully exercise the embedding-backed semantic predicates introduced in #67/#68.

rules.naturalLanguage: Architecture must address: Shared Responsibility Model
rules.lambda: SemanticFunctions.MatchesAnyMeaning(input1.id, "shared responsibility|CSP responsibilities|cloud consumer accountability|security obligations split|provider versus customer security", 0.55)
rules.remediation: Add a section to the architecture document covering "Shared Responsibility Model". Define which security controls are owned by the cloud provider versus the customer. (Reference: ARB Cloud Security Directive — Support).

positive: The organization has established contracts with its cloud service providers that detail the security obligations of both parties.
To comply with security standards, the Organization Cloud Consumer must have agreements in place that specify security responsibilities.
It is essential for the Organization to ensure that all third-party service contracts include clear security provisions.
negative: The shared responsibility model outlines the roles of the Organization and the CSP in cloud security.
Refer to the glossary for definitions related to cloud security responsibilities.
The document discusses various cloud service models without specifying obligations for the Organization Cloud Consumer.

rules.naturalLanguage: Architecture must address: Governance
rules.lambda: SemanticFunctions.MatchesAnyMeaning(input1.id, "cloud governance|steering committee|architecture review board|approval workflow|cloud strategy|onboarding governance", 0.55)
rules.remediation: Add a section to the architecture document covering "Governance". Document the governance body, approval flow, and architecture-review process for cloud workloads. (Reference: ARB Cloud Security Directive — Security and Governance).

positive: The organization has implemented a process to conduct thorough Third-Party Security Assessments in accordance with the Third-Party Risk Management Policy.
As part of our compliance efforts, we ensure that all third-party suppliers undergo security assessments as mandated by our risk management guidelines.
Regular third-party security evaluations are conducted to align with the Organization’s Third-Party Risk Management Policy.
negative: The Third-Party Risk Management Policy outlines various security measures but does not specify assessment requirements.
In our organization, we discuss third-party risks in meetings but do not have a formal assessment process in place.
The policy mentions the importance of third-party security but lacks details on how assessments should be conducted.

rules.naturalLanguage: Architecture must address: Roles and Accountabilities
rules.lambda: SemanticFunctions.MatchesAnyMeaning(input1.id, "RACI matrix|roles and responsibilities|accountable owner|DRI|operations accountability|security accountability", 0.55)
rules.remediation: Add a section to the architecture document covering "Roles and Accountabilities". Specify named owners (RACI) for each layer of the architecture: app team, platform team, security team, CSP. (Reference: ARB Cloud Security Directive — Operational Excellence).

positive: The Organization Cloud Consumer is responsible for ensuring that all cloud services meet the required security standards as outlined in the directives.
During the implementation of cloud services, the Organization Cloud Consumer must verify compliance with security controls.
It is the duty of the Organization Cloud Consumer to manage risk by adhering to the security directives during cloud operations.
negative: The roles and accountabilities section outlines various responsibilities without specifying compliance requirements.
The Organization Cloud Consumer refers to the role in the context of cloud services but does not mention security controls.
In the guidelines, the first line of defence is discussed without detailing the obligations of the Organization Cloud Consumer.

rules.naturalLanguage: Architecture must address: Asset Management in the Cloud
rules.lambda: SemanticFunctions.MatchesAnyMeaning(input1.id, "cloud asset inventory|tagging strategy|resource tagging|asset register|data classification labels|CMDB", 0.55)
rules.remediation: Add a section to the architecture document covering "Asset Management in the Cloud". Define mandatory resource tags (owner, environment, data-classification, cost-center) and an asset inventory mechanism. (Reference: ARB Cloud Security Directive — Cost Optimization).

positive: The organization has implemented tagging for all cloud-based assets to ensure they are properly inventoried.
According to the Asset Management Directive, all cloud assets must be tracked and managed effectively.
Regular audits confirm that the organization’s cloud assets are inventoried and protected as per the established guidelines.
negative: The asset management policy outlines various controls but does not specify cloud-based assets.
Refer to the glossary for definitions related to asset management in cloud environments.
The organization is exploring options for improving data quality in cloud storage without committing to specific inventory practices.

rules.naturalLanguage: Architecture must address: Access Control
rules.lambda: SemanticFunctions.MatchesAnyMeaning(input1.id, "least privilege|just-in-time access|role-based access control|conditional access|privileged identity management|Entra ID groups|zero trust", 0.55)
rules.remediation: Add a section to the architecture document covering "Access Control". Apply least-privilege RBAC, JIT/PIM elevation, and conditional access for all human and service principals. (Reference: ARB Cloud Security Directive — Security and Governance).

positive: The cloud service provider must comply with the Organization's Logical Access Security Directive to ensure proper user access management.
User access must be managed according to the Organization's policies, ensuring that only authorized personnel have access to sensitive information.
The Organization requires that all user accounts are managed in compliance with established logical access policies.
negative: The Organization's Logical Access Security Directive outlines various security measures for data protection.
User Access Management is a critical aspect of security but is not explicitly defined in this section.
Access control measures are discussed in the context of general security practices without specific obligations.

rules.naturalLanguage: Architecture must address: Cryptography
rules.lambda: SemanticFunctions.MatchesAnyMeaning(input1.id, "encryption at rest|encryption in transit|TLS 1.2|customer-managed keys|key vault|Key Vault|HSM|key rotation", 0.55)
rules.remediation: Add a section to the architecture document covering "Cryptography". Encrypt data at rest with customer-managed keys (Key Vault / HSM) and enforce TLS 1.2+ in transit. (Reference: ARB Cloud Security Directive — Security and Governance).

positive: The organization has implemented cryptographic controls that meet the strength requirements outlined in the Cryptography Directive.
To protect sensitive data, the cloud service employs cryptographic measures that effectively mitigate identified risks.
All cryptographic controls in our cloud services align with the security requirements specified in the relevant directives.
negative: The Cryptography Directive provides guidelines for cryptographic practices but does not specify mandatory controls.
In our cloud environment, we discuss various cryptographic technologies without committing to specific strength requirements.
The document outlines the importance of cryptography but lacks details on the strength of controls to be implemented.

rules.naturalLanguage: Architecture must address: Operations Security
rules.lambda: SemanticFunctions.MatchesAnyMeaning(input1.id, "patch management|vulnerability scanning|Defender for Cloud|SIEM integration|incident response|Sentinel|anti-malware", 0.55)
rules.remediation: Add a section to the architecture document covering "Operations Security". Wire workloads to centralised SIEM/Defender, run regular vuln scans, and define an incident-response runbook. (Reference: ARB Cloud Security Directive — Security and Governance).

positive: All changes to cloud applications are logged and monitored to ensure data integrity, with alerts sent to the organization immediately.
The organization has established procedures for detecting and logging any modifications to workloads in the cloud environment.
Change detection mechanisms are in place to track alterations in services, ensuring that integrity is maintained and reported.
negative: The change detection process is outlined in the IT Change Management Directive.
Logging procedures are mentioned in the context of general security practices without specific obligations.
The document discusses the importance of data integrity but does not specify requirements for logging changes.

rules.naturalLanguage: Architecture must address: Security Requirements for Cloud Service Providers
rules.lambda: SemanticFunctions.MatchesAnyMeaning(input1.id, "CSP attestation|SOC 2|ISO 27001|FedRAMP|third-party risk|vendor security review|data processing agreement|PCI", 0.55)
rules.evidenceQuote: Security Requirements for Cloud Service Providers
rules.remediation: Add a section to the architecture document covering "Security Requirements for Cloud Service Providers". Cite the CSP's attestations (SOC 2 / ISO 27001 / FedRAMP) and the contractual security clauses relied upon. (Reference: ARB Cloud Security Directive — Security and Governance).

metadata.sourcePolicy: Security Requirements for Cloud Service Providers

rules.naturalLanguage: Architecture must address: Compliance Monitoring
rules.lambda: SemanticFunctions.MatchesAnyMeaning(input1.id, "continuous compliance|Azure Policy|compliance dashboard|drift detection|audit logs|activity log|control monitoring", 0.55)
rules.remediation: Add a section to the architecture document covering "Compliance Monitoring". Enable Azure Policy / continuous compliance monitoring and route audit logs to a tamper-evident store. (Reference: ARB Cloud Security Directive — Monitoring).

positive: The Directive Sponsor submitted the annual report detailing compliance status and the effectiveness of the Directive.
Each year, the Directive Sponsor provides an update on compliance and the effectiveness of the Directive to the relevant stakeholders.
The annual compliance report from the Directive Sponsor includes an assessment of how well the Directive is being followed.
negative: The compliance monitoring process is outlined in the Directive and includes various guidelines.
Business Group leaders are responsible for identifying non-compliance areas but do not report annually.
The Directive Sponsor will leverage documented processes for compliance assessment but does not specify reporting frequency.

rules.naturalLanguage: Architecture must address: Security Exceptions
rules.lambda: SemanticFunctions.MatchesAnyMeaning(input1.id, "security exception process|risk acceptance|compensating control|exception register|time-bound waiver", 0.55)
rules.remediation: Add a section to the architecture document covering "Security Exceptions". Document any deviations as time-bound exceptions with compensating controls, owner, and review date. (Reference: ARB Cloud Security Directive — Security and Governance).

positive: A Security Exception was submitted due to the technical limitations preventing compliance with the encryption requirements.
The organization filed a Policy Exception Request to address the business reasons for not meeting the data retention policy.
In light of the cost to remediate, a Security Waiver was approved after reviewing the associated risks.
negative: The Security Exception Request Process outlines the steps for submitting a request.
Definitions of Security Exceptions can be found in the glossary section of the document.
The directive mentions that some organizations may face challenges in compliance without committing to a Security Exception.

rules.naturalLanguage: Architecture must address: Implementation
rules.lambda: SemanticFunctions.MatchesAnyMeaning(input1.id, "change management|release approval|deployment pipeline|rollback plan|blue-green deployment|change advisory board", 0.55)
rules.remediation: Add a section to the architecture document covering "Implementation". Define the deployment / change-management process with approvals, rollback, and CAB review. (Reference: ARB Cloud Security Directive — Operational Excellence).

positive: The Organization has established a comprehensive security program that is overseen globally by the Security Risk Policy Co-Sponsors, with the CISO providing necessary assistance.
In accordance with the directives, the Organization's security program is managed under the guidance of the Security Risk Policy Co-Sponsors and supported by the CISO.
The security program includes global oversight by designated Co-Sponsors and is actively supported by the Chief Information Security Officer.
negative: The Security Risk Policy outlines various aspects of security management without detailing the oversight structure.
For more information on security risk management, refer to the guidelines provided in the Security Risk Policy.
The Organization's approach to security is discussed in the context of risk management frameworks without specifying the roles of the Co-Sponsors or CISO.

rules.naturalLanguage: Architecture must address: Architect for Stability and Resiliency by design
rules.lambda: SemanticFunctions.MatchesAnyMeaning(input1.id, "high availability|fault tolerance|resiliency|availability zones|multi-region|RTO|RPO|disaster recovery|graceful degradation", 0.55)
rules.evidenceQuote: Architect for Stability and Resiliency by design
rules.remediation: Add a section to the architecture document covering "Architect for Stability and Resiliency by design". Specify HA topology (AZs / multi-region), measured RTO/RPO targets, and DR runbook. (Reference: ARB Cloud Security Directive — Reliability).

metadata.sourcePolicy: Architect for Stability and Resiliency by design

rules.naturalLanguage: Architecture must address: Compliance by design
rules.lambda: SemanticFunctions.MatchesAnyMeaning(input1.id, "compliance by design|privacy by design|regulatory mapping|GDPR|HIPAA|FINTRAC|data residency", 0.55)
rules.remediation: Add a section to the architecture document covering "Compliance by design". Map the design to applicable regulations (GDPR / HIPAA / data-residency) and embed controls up-front. (Reference: ARB Cloud Security Directive — Security and Governance).

positive: During the design phase, we integrated risk assessments to ensure all features align with our corporate risk strategy.
The project plan includes a risk-aligned mitigation strategy that outlines an exit strategy as a contingency.
All new features are designed with risk considerations in mind, allowing for agile execution while managing potential risks.
negative: The compliance by design approach emphasizes the importance of risk management in technology solutions.
Refer to the glossary for definitions related to risk management and compliance.
The document discusses various risk strategies without committing to specific design obligations.

rules.naturalLanguage: Architecture must address: Security by design
rules.lambda: SemanticFunctions.MatchesAnyMeaning(input1.id, "security by design|threat model|STRIDE|attack surface|secure SDLC|SAST DAST|penetration testing", 0.55)
rules.remediation: Add a section to the architecture document covering "Security by design". Include a threat model (STRIDE) and integrate SAST/DAST + pen testing into the SDLC. (Reference: ARB Cloud Security Directive — Security and Governance).

positive: The design document includes a section on cybersecurity measures that will be implemented to protect client data from unauthorized access.
Incorporating security features from the outset ensures that data integrity is maintained throughout the application lifecycle.
The team has engaged cybersecurity experts during the design phase to address potential vulnerabilities in the solution.
negative: Cybersecurity is an important aspect of IT solutions, but it is often discussed in later stages of development.
The document outlines various features of the solution without mentioning how security will be integrated.
Appendix A provides definitions of cybersecurity terms but does not specify how they will be applied in the design process.

rules.naturalLanguage: Architecture must address: Cloud First design
rules.lambda: SemanticFunctions.MatchesAnyMeaning(input1.id, "cloud-first|PaaS-first|managed services|serverless|platform-as-a-service|cloud-native", 0.55)
rules.remediation: Add a section to the architecture document covering "Cloud First design". Default to managed PaaS / serverless services rather than IaaS or self-hosted equivalents. (Reference: ARB Cloud Security Directive — Portability and Modularization).

positive: The organization has decided to prioritize cloud solutions for projects that demonstrate significant cost savings and scalability.
In our strategy, we will invest in cloud technologies where they provide a clear business advantage, such as faster recovery times.
The business case for adopting a multi-cloud strategy was presented, highlighting the benefits of flexibility and cost efficiency.
negative: The cloud-first design approach is a guideline for modern IT strategies.
Refer to the section on cloud maturity for definitions and examples.
The document outlines various cloud technologies without committing to specific business cases.

rules.naturalLanguage: Architecture must address: API First design
rules.lambda: SemanticFunctions.MatchesAnyMeaning(input1.id, "API-first|OpenAPI|REST contract|API gateway|contract-driven|Swagger", 0.55)
rules.remediation: Add a section to the architecture document covering "API First design". Publish OpenAPI / Swagger contracts and front services with an API-gateway / management layer. (Reference: ARB Cloud Security Directive — Portability and Modularization).

positive: The organization has implemented an enterprise-wide API governance framework that standardizes API development and ensures interoperability across systems.
To modernize our legacy systems, we have defined clear API standards and an operating model that guides our integration efforts.
Our API strategy includes comprehensive documentation of interfaces and contracts to facilitate seamless information exchange.
negative: API governance refers to the policies and standards that guide API development and usage.
The document outlines various API technologies without committing to a specific operating model.
In the context of API design, it is important to consider the separation of concerns between presentation and business logic.

rules.naturalLanguage: Architecture must address: DevOps Automation
rules.lambda: SemanticFunctions.MatchesAnyMeaning(input1.id, "DevOps|CI/CD|continuous integration|continuous deployment|Azure DevOps|GitHub Actions|pipeline automation|infrastructure as code", 0.55)
rules.remediation: Add a section to the architecture document covering "DevOps Automation". Automate build / test / deploy through CI/CD pipelines with infrastructure-as-code (Terraform / Bicep). (Reference: ARB Cloud Security Directive — Operational Excellence).

positive: All production deployments must be automated; manual deployments are only allowed in rare and documented cases.
The policy states that manual deployments to production are prohibited unless there are exceptional circumstances that justify it.
In our organization, we strictly enforce that production environments are only updated through automated processes, with manual exceptions being extremely rare.
negative: The DevOps pipeline has shown improvements in efficiency and cost reduction.
Maturing our DevOps pipelines includes various initiatives across all platforms.
DevOps metrics indicate a significant reduction in development cycles and delivery costs, but manual deployments are sometimes necessary.

rules.naturalLanguage: Architecture must address: Scalabilty and Reusability
rules.lambda: SemanticFunctions.MatchesAnyMeaning(input1.id, "horizontal scaling|auto-scaling|reusable component|stateless service|scale-out|load balancer|elasticity", 0.55)
rules.remediation: Add a section to the architecture document covering "Scalabilty and Reusability". Design stateless, horizontally-scalable services with auto-scale rules and shared reusable components. (Reference: ARB Cloud Security Directive — Performance and Efficiency).

positive: The architecture is designed to be highly scalable, allowing for both scaling up and scaling down as needed to maintain efficiency.
We ensure data consistency across systems while adapting to changes in requirements with a flexible architecture.
Our engineering team is skilled in implementing event-driven architecture to enhance scalability and maintain data integrity.
negative: Scalability refers to the ability of a system to handle growth in workload without compromising performance.
The document outlines various technologies that can be used for cloud architecture without committing to specific scalability requirements.
In the glossary, scalability is defined as the capacity to increase resources as demand grows, but no obligations are stated.

rules.naturalLanguage: Architecture must address: Modularize
rules.lambda: SemanticFunctions.MatchesAnyMeaning(input1.id, "modular design|microservices|loosely coupled|bounded context|separation of concerns|service decomposition", 0.55)
rules.remediation: Add a section to the architecture document covering "Modularize". Decompose into loosely-coupled modules / microservices with well-defined boundaries. (Reference: ARB Cloud Security Directive — Portability & Modularization).

positive: The architecture utilizes modular components that can be independently replaced, allowing for easier updates and maintenance.
By implementing a modular design, we can adapt to technological changes without overhauling the entire system.
Our system architecture is structured around independent modules that facilitate re-use and simplify complexity management.
negative: Modularization is a concept that refers to the design of systems in separate components.
The document outlines various architectural styles, including modular architecture.
Flexibility in business operations can be enhanced through various strategies, including modularization.

rules.naturalLanguage: Architecture must address: Maximize value
rules.lambda: SemanticFunctions.MatchesAnyMeaning(input1.id, "cost optimization|FinOps|reserved instances|right-sizing|cost governance|spending alerts|value realization|TCO", 0.55)
rules.remediation: Add a section to the architecture document covering "Maximize value". Apply FinOps controls: cost alerts, right-sizing, reserved capacity, tagging-driven chargeback. (Reference: ARB Cloud Security Directive — Cost Optimization).

positive: The organization evaluates all technology investments against their risk profile to ensure maximum value is achieved.
A holistic assessment is conducted before selecting new technologies to ensure they align with business requirements and do not duplicate existing capabilities.
To minimize costs, the company has phased out older technologies in favor of newer solutions that provide overlapping functionalities.
negative: The principles of cost management are discussed in the context of maximizing value.
This section outlines the importance of technology in achieving business goals without committing to specific investment strategies.
The document mentions various technologies but does not specify any obligations regarding their assessment or investment criteria.
